description: BGPStream is an open-source software framework for analysing historical and real-time Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) measurement data. Its C library libBGPStream and command-line tool bgpreader give a single sorted stream of BGP updates and routing table dumps from collectors such as RouteViews and RIPE RIS, with filters by project, collector, prefix, peer, AS path and time; the PyBGPStream Python bindings and real-time data brokers let researchers build monitoring and analysis pipelines. It is developed by the Center for Applied Internet Data Analysis (CAIDA) at the University of California San Diego; the newest release tag is v2.3.0. Coverage: global Internet routing as seen by public collectors, from the early 2000s to near real time, at the resolution of individual BGP messages. Format and access: source tarballs and packages from the website and GitHub, reading MRT data over the Internet; free of charge under a BSD-style licence from the Regents of the University of California. Caveats: it processes data but stores none, so results depend on collector coverage and availability; very long historical queries are slow. Simulation uses: building event records of outages and hijacks for resilience and cascading-failure studies, network flow inputs for Internet topology models, and real-time monitoring for emergency response. Related records: RIPE RIS, RouteViews and CAIDA AS relationships are its data sources and companions, IODA uses it for outage detection, and C-BGP can replay its routes.
